# Isolde Pembroke

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an attractive girl with black hair, dark eyes, and rosy cheeks. She possesses a high complexion and vigor, along with dark ringlets. Though described as short and plump like a dumpling, she carries a bright and lovely appearance, often wearing a crimson ulster or gingham dress.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c17 P10](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0010), [v1 c25 P40](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0040), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c33 P13](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0013), [v2 c2 P15](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0015), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039)_

## Personality

Cheerful, sweet, and kind, Isolde is an exceptionally comforting companion who brings moral support and comfort to those around her. She is practical, down-to-earth, and practical-minded, though she occasionally harbors secret skepticism toward grand imaginations. She can also be determined and firm, such as refusing to speak to schoolmates who act dishonestly.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026), [v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017), [v1 c37 P19](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0019), [v1 c37 P21](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0021), [v2 c6 P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002), [v2 c13 P4](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0004), [v2 c14 P49](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0049)_

## History

Isolde spent her early years living at Pear Hill, visiting her aunt in Delford during childhood before returning home to become acquainted with Nell Harcourt. The two young girls formed a close bond, establishing a playhouse named Larkrise and attending Brierley school together. Isolde participated in school events, including performing a vocal solo at a town concert, and later traveled to town to stay with her Aunt Lavinia for the Exhibition. As she grew older, she joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society, taking on the role of treasurer and providing moral support to committee projects. She later became engaged to Gideon Duckett under the willow tree in her family garden.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P8](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0008), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c25 P50](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0050), [v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c14 P49](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0049), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- received her name because a schoolmaster lodged at her home when she was born  <sub>[v1 c2 P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064)</sub>

## Quotes

> Every one of those Tulk girls acts dishonestly. Yesterday, Tibby Tulk literally set her milk bottle where mine belonged in the brook. Can you imagine? Now I refuse to talk to her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)</sub>

> Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.  <sub>[v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)</sub>

> I should certainly think not. If he had, I would hardly be prone to brag about it, that terrible creature! I was certain it was beyond your guessing. Mother received a missive from Aunt Lavinia today, in which Aunt Lavinia requests that you and I travel to town this coming Tuesday and remain at her place for the Exhibition. So there!  <sub>[v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011)</sub>

> Trees don’t possess souls, yet the aroma of dead fir is undeniably wonderful. I intend to craft a cushion and stuff it with needles from the firs. You ought to craft one as well, Nell.  <sub>[v2 c6 P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002)</sub>

> Being engaged to Gideon is absolutely wonderful . . . however, being engaged to anybody else would be downright terrible, in my opinion.  <sub>[v2 c29 P18](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0018)</sub>
